rules.statement: A change that adds or renames a field or an event in a documented record contract, such as an audit record, updates that contract's document in the same change.
rules.why: The document is the reviewed contract that log pipelines, trace backends and incident runbooks are built against.
rules.check: Look for new or renamed audit field-name constants, record members or event names in the diff with no matching edit to the contract document.

rules.statement: Never put a token, an authorization code, a credential, a secret or a request query string into an audit record, including its error message and its event-specific details.
rules.why: An audit record carries identifiers and metadata only; query strings can carry codes or tokens.
rules.check: Look at audit event details, error messages and request capture for token values, codes, secrets, passwords, full URLs or QueryString use.

rules.statement: When recording a request path for audit or telemetry, use PathBase plus Path and never include the query string.
rules.why: The query string can carry authorization codes or tokens.
rules.check: Look for Request.QueryString, GetDisplayUrl, GetEncodedUrl or full URI values written into audit or telemetry fields.

rules.statement: In an audit record, omit a member that has no value, and omit an empty resources array, instead of writing null or an empty array.
rules.why: The record contract says absent members are omitted, never written as null.
rules.check: Look for WriteNull or unconditional property writes of nullable values and empty arrays in the audit record writer or in ISupportAuditDetails implementations.

rules.statement: Model audit vocabularies such as outcomes, severities, categories, sources, actor types and resource types as open sets of lower-case string names, not as enums.
rules.why: Per ADR-1150, a package that adds an event adds its own names without editing the library.
rules.check: Look for new enums or closed switch statements over audit vocabulary values, or vocabulary names that are not lower-case.

rules.statement: When a field is added to a released versioned record schema, bump the schema's minor version.
rules.why: The schema_version tells consumers which fields to expect; the contract says an added field bumps the minor version.
rules.check: Look for a new field in the audit record writer without a change to the SchemaVersion constant.

rules.statement: Give metric attributes only bounded, low-cardinality values; never put identifiers, free-form names or other unbounded values on a metric.
rules.why: The audit metric carries only event_name, event_category and outcome; bounded values such as an environment type are used, never a free-form environment name.
rules.check: Look at tags added to counters or histograms for ids, user names, client ids, paths, messages or free-form names.

rules.statement: Use the same audit field names in the record, the log state, the span tags and the metric attributes, taken from the declared field-name constants instead of string literals.
rules.why: An operator pivots between a log entry, its trace and the counters without translating names.
rules.check: Look for audit field names written as string literals, or a log, span or metric field whose name differs from the record field name apart from its audit. or metric prefix.

rules.statement: Have each audit event state its actor and its event category explicitly, rather than deriving the actor from how the request authenticated or the category from the event name's prefix.
rules.why: The actor must not depend on how a request authenticated, and names such as client.authentication and client.created share a prefix but have different categories.
rules.check: Look for actor types taken from the authentication scheme or principal type, or categories computed by splitting the event name.

rules.statement: Generate audit event identifiers as UUIDv7 and write event times in UTC in RFC 3339 format with a Z suffix.
rules.why: UUIDv7 identifiers sort by time and index and paginate well; the contract fixes event_time as UTC with a Z suffix.
rules.check: Look for Guid.NewGuid() used for event ids, or event times that are local or written with an offset instead of Z.

rules.statement: Truncate a captured User-Agent header to 512 characters before writing it into an audit record.
rules.why: The contract cuts the user agent at 512 characters, which limits the size of an untrusted header in the record.
rules.check: Look for User-Agent capture with no length limit.

rules.statement: Set an audit event's error code to a stable, machine-readable value, the OAuth error code where one applies, and keep human-readable text in the message.
rules.why: error.code is for filtering and pivoting, so it must stay stable.
rules.check: Look for error codes built from exception messages or other free text, or a custom code used where an OAuth error code applies.
